method: Direct visual inspection of decoded local image files after pHash/SIFT candidate discovery; no replacement or deletion performed.
limitations: Shared background lineage is not proof that two whole artworks are identical. Narrative variants below require policy adjudication before counting as separate originals.

findings.observation: Identical Christ portrait, clothing, hair, horizon and sunset. Different size/encoding does not create new original artwork.
Same riverbank and John identity; witness scene points toward Christ with disciples, question scene replaces foreground visitors and changes John's gesture. Not merely crop or rename.
Same courtyard and host; closed door with empty basket becomes open door with neighbor supplying bread. Substantive story action changes.
Same rocky road and wounded traveler; later scene adds kneeling Samaritan and changes traveler's head and posture to respond. Substantive story action changes.

Same palace, guards and king; foreground changes from kneeling plea to rising pardoned servant, then two reporting witnesses. King gesture changes for pardon. Substantial background reuse; whole scenes are not identical.
